deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

items.rationale: Lists the IP ranges/CIDRs that make up the address group used in network rules. A policy can usefully require these entries to avoid overly broad ranges (e.g. disallow 0.0.0.0/0) to limit network exposure; it must not hardcode one team's specific CIDR.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the AddressGroup resource.
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.

location.description:
The location of the gateway security policy.
The default value is 'global'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

parent.description: The name of the parent this address group belongs to. Format: organizations/{organization_id} or projects/{project_id}.

type.description: The type of the Address Group. Possible values are "IPV4" or "IPV6". Possible values: ["IPV4", "IPV6"]
type.rationale: Declares the IP family (IPV4/IPV6) of the address group's entries. The address family is a structural/networking choice with no security advantage of one over the other, so mandating IPV4 is an arbitrary constraint rather than a security control.
